topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with introductory remarks and an outline of learning objectives concerning cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Fundamental Drivers and Origins of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by endogenous errors, DNA repair capacity, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental risk factors alongside the epidemiological evidence and debates regarding preventable versus chance mutations.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, using the interaction between Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma as a primary model.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which physical radiation and metabolically activated chemicals induce direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze non-mutagenic tumor promoters, the multi-stage model of carcinogenesis, and the impact of host developmental timing on cancer risk.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic signatures, epidemiological approaches, and experimental assays used to establish carcinogenic potential and weigh environmental risks.
